Chapter 10: Paying It Forward—Mentoring and Supporting Others
So, we’ve come a long way together—and here’s where it all comes full circle. The last step in this journey? Taking what you’ve learned, all the ups and downs, and using that wisdom to help others grow.
Think about it: when you mentor, sponsor, or advocate for someone else, you’re not just building them up—you’re actually reinforcing your own growth and becoming a stronger leader yourself.
Now, mentoring isn’t just about giving advice. It’s about being present, really listening, and asking those thoughtful questions that help someone figure out their own path. Sometimes, just being a sounding board can help someone discover strengths they didn’t even know they had.
Sponsorship? That takes things up a notch. It means you’re willing to use your influence to open doors for someone—maybe recommending them for a big project, or introducing them to people who can help them shine.
If you’re looking for ways to truly pay it forward, here are a few ideas:
Offer guidance and encouragement to folks going through challenges you remember facing.
Don’t be shy about sharing your lessons learned—yes, both the wins and the times you stumbled. It helps everyone see that growth is a process, not a straight line.
Speak up when you see a chance to make opportunities more equitable for your team. And don’t forget to model the values and behaviors that make your workplace a welcoming, inclusive space.
Picture this: a senior leader spots real potential in a team member. Instead of just cheering from the sidelines, she goes a step further—she recommends this person for a high-visibility project, or introduces her to people who can open new doors. That simple act? It doesn’t just boost one career. It sparks new energy and diversity across the whole organization.
Here’s something important to remember—supporting others isn’t a one-way street. It sets off a ripple effect, strengthening the entire community around you. When you invest in the growth of your colleagues, you’re building a legacy—a culture of empowerment and positive change that keeps on giving.
